newsitem.title: USA: Lee County, S.C., approves school bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Lee County, S.C., approves school bond issues.

text.p: Voters in South Carolina's Lee County approved two general obligation bond issues totalling $16.5 million, elections officials said.
A $15 million issue to build a new, consolidated high school passed with 56 percent of the votes cast in Saturday's referendum.
A $1.5 million issue to build a gym and auditorium passed with 54 percent of the votes.

The referendum was the first for school bonds in the poor, rural county. Supporters attributed the bond approval to heavy turnout among blacks, who make up 90 percent of the public school population, but only 62 percent of the overall population.
The proposal will raise property taxes by 39 percent, to $125 a year for the owner of a $50,000 home.
